summary: A call needed a capability the manifest does not declare.
The manifest declares the capability and the owner has not granted it.
The call fell outside the scope the owner consented to.
The publisher's trust level is below the capability's floor.
A guest brought a plugin holding a capability whose effect does not reverse when the guest leaves.
The plugin asked the host container for a service. The contract has facades instead.
The plugin used the raw event bus. The contract has a topic list instead.
The plugin put a bearer token in a media URL. The host mints every media URL.
The plugin read or wrote a folder the owner has not granted.
The plugin started a process without process.spawn.
The plugin's child process would have run outside the plugin's own sandbox.
The plugin opened a raw socket without network.dial.
The plugin bound a listening socket without network.listen.
The request went to a host outside the glob the owner granted.
The plugin claimed a route under the underscore prefix the host owns.
The caller does not hold the access the route declares.
The manifest targets an ABI this server does not load.
The manifest does not match the schema the server reads.
The plugin depends on another plugin the server does not have.
The plugin depends on a paid plugin this server does not own.
A free plugin depends on a paid one, which the marketplace does not allow.
The plugin a dependency points at is paused, so the call has nothing to reach.
The cross-plugin contract version the caller asks for is not the one the provider offers.
The call needs a user scope and ran without one.
The plugin sent user data to a host outside the server.
A capability that reads a person's own data was called with nobody asking.
The plugin wrote a settings field its schema marks read only.
A secret was written into settings, where it would be readable. Secrets live in the secret store.
The plugin is at its disk quota, so the write has nowhere to go.
A device on the network used a credential the server does not know, or one the owner revoked.
The router refused to forward the port, which no change to the plugin can fix.
No router on this network answered a port-forwarding request.
A supervised worker crashed and the host restarted it.
The live link the plugin published stopped answering.
The recording stopped because the disk it writes to is full.
The stream carries a codec the remuxer cannot repackage.
The headless browser navigated to a host outside the granted scope.
The plugin asked the user for input without ui.input.
The native library the plugin loads carries no signature this server trusts.
A hub method was reached on a connection the host could not resolve a caller for.
A per-user secret was reached on a call with no resolved caller.
This exact build was revoked, so it does not run.
The server has not reached the revocation list in over a week, so it cannot say a plugin is still allowed.
A paid plugin, and the server owner holds no entitlement for it.
The server could not confirm a purchase for over a week, so the plugin is installed and not running.
An offline bundle that NoMercy did not sign, or that was edited after signing.
An offline bundle older than the validity it was issued with.
Installing a plugin from a file is off, because the server cannot check who wrote it.
The id belongs to a paid plugin and the owner holds no entitlement for it.
The plugin is not shared with the account asking for it on this server.
A media link the server minted has run out, or was never one it minted.
A media link minted for one account was used by another.
A plugin offered a file to a library it may not write to, or from a path outside one.
A plugin went past the CPU or memory the owner allowed it, and the server acted.
A plugin was restarted too many times in an hour, so the server stopped restarting it.
A plugin is sending faster than the share of the uplink the owner allowed it.
